references.text: The introduction to the chapter warns Israel against following the customs of the Egyptians and Canaanites, which is the context for the defilement mentioned in verse 24.
Continues the theme that the land will vomit out its inhabitants because of their impurities and abominations.
A parallel warning to keep God's laws so that the land does not vomit them out, and not to follow the customs of the nations.
Explains that it is because of the wickedness of the nations that the Lord drives them out before Israel.
Warning against imitating the detestable practices of the displaced nations.
Lists the abominations practiced by the peoples in Canaan, which led to their being driven out.
God tells Abraham that the sin of the Amorites is not yet complete, pointing toward future judgment on the nations.
Israel themselves became unclean and were judged because they followed the customs of the nations.
Describes how Israel mixed with the nations, learned their deeds, and became unclean.
